newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds recover, turnover unimpressive.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds recover, turnover unimpressive.

text.p: *Australian bonds extended Tuesday's rebound in early trading, spurred on by a more stable U.S. Treasury market, but once again turnover was far from impressive.
*No local data, but Japan releases Q2 Tankan survey.
Australian bond futures extended Tuesday's rebound, spurred on by a more stable U.S. Treasury market, but once again turnover was far from impressive.
Traders said the market is largely marking time ahead of next week's policy making meetings in both Australian and the U.S., and in the absence of any key local data.
"I can't see us doing a lot today. There are some figures out of the U.S. tonight and the Tankan in our trading time, but other than that we wait for the meetings," one trader said.
Japan releases its second quarter Tankan survey at 2350 GMT (9.50 a.m. Sydney time).

Futures contracts remain close to their recent highs on the expectation that the Reserve Bank will ease policy after its July 1 board meeting and as long as the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1-2 keeps policy on hold.

"The market has a 50 basis point rate cut marked in, so the risk/reward has to be on the downside, that is if rates remain on hold and retail trade (next week) comes in higher than expectations," one trader said.
Retail trade recorded its first back to falls for three years in March/April, suggesting that the series for May, due on July 2, is due for a correction, he added.

U.S. Treasuries showed modest gains at Tuesday's New York close after a reasonably well received two-year note sale and after overcoming a weaker tone that followed a rise to a 28-year high in the June Conference Board consumer confidence index.
The index rose to 129.6 from a revised 127.9 in May.
The U.S. faces May durable goods orders and existing home sales for same period later on Wednesday.

The local market clawed back Tuesday's spread widening against the U.S. and Canada, but again lagged New Zealand debt. The N.Z. market is taking a positive approach to this Thursday's budget and was further boosted by a Eurokiwi issue on Tuesday. The Canadian market was flat.
